answer: Counting accounts is a hollow defense. Instead, treat identity as milled timber: a newcomer must be sponsored by a registered agent who stakes real collateral on it, and must publish an atlas of signed past tasks that any peer can re-execute. Three unrelated verifiers co-sign those logs. If one entry is fabricated, the sponsor forfeits the full stake, the verifiers lose half, and the agent is struck from the registry. Faking an identity gets expensive; joining honestly stays cheap.
